full_name: Schmidt Sciences — Science of Trustworthy AI (AI safety science program)
mission: Schmidt Sciences (founded by Eric and Wendy Schmidt) funds 'basic technical research that improves our ability to understand, predict, and control risks from frontier AI systems.' The program (launched as 'AI Safety Science', now 'Science of Trustworthy AI') backs academic and nonprofit researchers — e.g. Bengio, Gleave, Hendrycks, Owain Evans, Krueger, Kolter — on evaluations, misalignment, oversight of superhuman systems and multi-agent risk. Founding year is approximate for the program.

key_work.title: Science of Trustworthy AI research agenda
key_work.plain_summary: Three aims: characterise and forecast misalignment, develop generalisable measurement and interventions, and oversee superhuman and multi-agent AI.

key_work.title: Scaling AI Safety for a Multi-Agent World
key_work.plain_summary: Agenda on risks that only appear when many AI systems interact.

key_work.title: Inference-time compute safety projects
key_work.plain_summary: A funded cohort studying reasoning models: chain-of-thought faithfulness, reward hacking at inference time and whether CoT monitoring helps.

warnings.text: 'The science of trustworthy AI is nascent'; demonstrations of unsafe behaviour are isolated and mitigations don't generalise reliably (program page).
Today's evaluations often fail where needed most — under distribution shift, long-horizon interaction, tool use and optimisation pressure — and are easy to 'train to'.
Research capacity for trustworthy AI lags the pace of deployment; commercial incentives for foundational safety science are weak.

recommendations.text: Build a rigorous science of evaluation with construct and predictive validity and clear evidence standards for real-world decisions.
Give sustained, compute-backed support to academics, treating foundational safety science as a global public good.
Develop oversight and control methods for settings where humans can't directly check AI correctness.
